texts.facts: The present Dar (detailed accident report) arises out of road accident that occurred on 14.03.2019, in which the petitioner Anuj allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 14.03.2019, IO received intimation of an accident at ICD Gate, Tuglakabad Village, Red light where he found a motorcycle bearing no. DL- 3SDP-7700 and a truck bearing no. HR-38Q-2665 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) in accidental condition, in the middle of the red light. IO was informed that the victim had been taken to the hospital. In the hospital MLC of the injured was prepared where the doctor opined the injuries to be grievous in nature. An FIR no. 51/2019 was registered at PS Pul Prahladpur, u/s 279/338 of IPC and Anuj (Dar) vs Shahid (51/2019, Pul Prahlad Pur) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161993274/ 1 the matter was investigated. It is pursuant to the investigation that a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC was filed before Ld. MM and a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 3. In response to the DAR reply was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2 denying the factum of accident as well as pleading that it was the injured (driving motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SDP- 7700) who was rash and negligent in driving his vehicle. It is further pleaded that the offending vehicle is insured with MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 2 of 20 ss Respondent no.3 and that Respondent no.1 had a valid driving licence at the time of accident. As per reply filed by Respondent no.3 liability to indemnify Respondent no.2 or compensate the petitioner has been disowned on the ground that the Respondent no.2 committed breach of insurance policy as the offending vehicle was being plied without a valid fitness and in violation in terms of Insurance policy. 4. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 30.05.2019. OPP 2. OPP 3. Relief. 5. PW-1 petitioner/injured Anuj led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/1 and relied upon MLC as Ex.PW1/A, treatment record/discharge summary as Ex.PW1/B, follow up treatment record as Ex.PW1/C, Medical bills as Ex.PW1/D, DAR Ex.PW1/E, ID Card as Ex.PW1/F, Driving licence as Ex.PW1/G, PAN card and Adhaar Card as Ex.PW1/H and Ex.PW1/I respectively and 12th class certificate as Ex.PW1/J. PW-1 was not cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondents ASI Rajbir Singh was examined as PW-2 who deposed that he had lodged FIR in the present case u/s 239/337 of IPC and MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 3 of 20 ss upon obtaining result on MLC, added Section 338 of IPC. He deposed that at the time of accident he found motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SDP-7700 and truck bearing no. HR-38Q-2665 in accidental condition. He could not find any eye witness. Later, he received information from ESI Hospital but the injured was unfit for statement. He returned to the spot, impounded the offending vehicle and the motorcycle of the injured and arrested the driver of the offending vehicle. PW-2 was duly cross examined by Ld. counsel for Insurance company. 6. No evidence was led by the Respondents despite opportunity. 7. Final arguments in details were addressed by all the parties.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 4 of 20 ss Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. It has been held by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Kaushalpati Pandey vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd. (MAC.APP. 185/2020, decided on 09.11.2020) that absence of a valid fitness certificate, entitles the insurance company to recovery rights against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, on account of no valid fitness with the offending vehicle, Respondent no.3/Insurance company shall be entitled to recover the compensation awarded to the petitioner, from Respondent no.1 and Respondent no. 2. MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 7 of 20 ss 15. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. Anuj (Dar) vs Shahid (51/2019, Pul Prahlad Pur) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161993274/ 4 16. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 8 of 20 ss (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure; (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 16.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 16.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 16.7. 19. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport MACT No. 319/19 Anuj vs. Shahid Khan Page no. 13 of 20 ss decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 20. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". 26. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) Anuj (Dar) vs Shahid (51/2019, Pul Prahlad Pur) on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161993274/ 10 of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
